# Phase 0 Fixture Specification

**Covers:** kickoff deliverable 7. Described, not built.

Per GOAL, a lint rule without a failing fixture does not exist. This specifies one
workbook per rule that violates exactly that rule, plus one clean workbook that
passes all ten.

---

## Construction principles

**Fixtures are generated by script, not committed as binaries.** A committed
`.xlsx` cannot be reviewed in a pull request and cannot be diffed, which is the
same problem this whole library exists to solve. `tests/fixtures/build_fixtures.py`
writes them into a `tmp_path` at test time. Tests that need cached values call
`recalc` on that temp file (ADR-0004). There are no committed binary fixtures.

**The skip / exit-2 path is injected, not hoped for.** A test that needs
`SKIPPED` fails every recalc backend on purpose rather than relying on
"openpyxl wrote this and Excel never opened it" as the only way to reach exit 2.
That path still exists as a characterisation of a file that arrived with no
cache, but the CLI's default is to recalculate first.

**Each fixture must violate exactly one rule.** This is harder than it sounds and
is the main design constraint here. A file contrived to break XL002 will casually
break XL003 as well; text placed for XL004 lands inside a summed range and trips
XL005. Every fixture below is minimised against that. Tests assert the *complete*
finding set, not merely that the expected rule appears — otherwise a fixture
silently drifts into testing three rules at once and the isolation is lost.

**Every fixture is a plausible workbook, not a synthetic grid.** Three sheets,
real labels, a small period axis. A fixture that looks nothing like real work
tests the rule against a world the rule will never meet. All data is synthetic:
no client names, no real figures.

---

## The clean baseline

`clean_baseline.xlsx` — generated. Passes all ten rules, and every other fixture
is a single mutation of it. This keeps fixtures minimal by construction and makes
each test diff legible.

| Sheet | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Inputs` | Driver block. Each constant has a text label in the cell immediately to its left. Inputs styled with blue font *and* a light fill. A legend block naming input / calculation / link / check. |
| `Calc` | Period axis `FY26 FY27 FY28` in columns D:F, header row 3. One formula shape per run. No literals outside the allowlist. A `chk_total_tie` named range evaluating to 0. |
| `Summary` | Presentation block. Same period axis in the same columns D:F. Self-contained title, units and currency. |

Two variants of the baseline exist as *test modes*, not as committed files: lint
after recalc (full pass, exit 0) and lint with recalc backends forced to fail
(value-dependent rules `SKIPPED`, exit 2).

---

## One fixture per rule

### XL001 — unlabelled-named-constant

`Inputs!C4` holds `0.85`, a defined name `FTE_TARGET` points at it, `Calc!D7`
references `FTE_TARGET`, and `B4` — the label cell immediately to its left — is
blank. The expected finding names both the defined name and the referencing
formula cell.

*Isolation note:* the constant must be referenced by a formula that is otherwise
compliant, or XL002 fires too. Use `=K4*FTE_TARGET` with `K4` a clean reference.

*Negative case in the same fixture family:* a second defined name with a populated
label cell, which must **not** produce a finding. Without this, the test passes
for a rule that fires on every named range.

### XL002 — numeric-literal-in-formula

`Calc!D7` contains `=C7*0.85`. Expected: one finding, naming the literal `0.85`.

*Isolation note:* the same fixture must also contain the positional exemption
cases that must **not** fire — `=ROUND(C8,2)`, `=VLOOKUP(B8,Ref!A:C,3,FALSE)`, and
an allowlisted `=C9*12`. This is the rule most at risk of noise, so its fixture
carries the anti-noise cases with it.

### XL003 — mixed-formula-shape-in-run

`Calc` row 9 spans D:G. D9:F9 are `=D8*$C$4`; G9 is `=SUM(D9:F9)`. Expected: one
finding reporting the inferred run and both shapes.

*Isolation note:* this is the intended false positive. A total column at the end
of a run is legitimate practice and this fixture is indistinguishable from it
without a spec. That is the point — the fixture proves the rule fires, and the
reported run bounds are what let a reader dismiss it in one glance. If a
span-inference exception for trailing aggregates is added later, this fixture
becomes its regression test.

### XL004 — text-in-numeric-cell

Generated, then recalculated. `Calc!E12` has a currency number format and a
cached value of the string `"N/A - no FTE load"`. Expected: one finding at
`Calc!E12`.

*Isolation note:* `E12` must sit outside any summed range, or XL005 fires as well.
The two rules are tested on deliberately separate cells.

### XL005 — text-in-aggregated-range

Generated, then recalculated. `Calc!E14` holds a text cached value inside
`E10:E20`, and `Summary!D8` contains `=SUM(Calc!E10:E20)`. Expected: one finding
that names both the offending cell and the aggregate it breaks.

*Isolation note:* `E14` carries a *general* number format, so XL004 does not fire
on it. The pair (XL004, XL005) is the cleanest demonstration that the split was
worth making.

### XL006 — inconsistent-period-axis

`Calc` has `FY26 FY27 FY28` in D:F. `Summary` has the same three labels shifted to
E:G. Expected: one workbook-level finding naming both sheets and the column offset.

*Isolation note:* a third sheet with no period header must produce no finding,
proving the rule is conditional on detection rather than firing on every sheet.

### XL101 — estimated-section-count

`Calc` carries seven label-plus-data groups separated by single blank rows,
against a default estimate budget of five. Expected: one WARN, explicitly marked
HEURISTIC and stating the estimate.

### XL102 — no-check-convention-found

`clean_baseline.xlsx` with the `chk_total_tie` named range removed and no
check-labelled row anywhere. Expected: one workbook-level WARN.

### XL103 — check-not-passing

Generated, then recalculated. `chk_total_tie` present with a cached value of
`1450`. Expected: one WARN naming the check and its value.

*Companion:* the same workbook with every recalc backend forced to fail, which
must produce `SKIPPED` and exit 2 — never a pass. This pair is the regression
test for the most dangerous failure mode in Phase 0.

### XL104 — input-styling-not-redundant

`Inputs!C4` is a constant that `Calc` depends on, styled with default font and no
fill, visually identical to the formula cells on `Calc`. Expected: one WARN.

---

## Fixtures for the machinery, not the rules

Four more, because the report contract needs testing as much as the rules do.

| Fixture | Tests |
|---|---|
| `no_cached_values.xlsx` (generated, recalc forced to fail) | Every `CACHED_VALUES` rule returns `SKIPPED`; exit code is 2, not 0 |
| `empty.xlsx` (one empty sheet) | No rule crashes on an empty used range; output is well-formed |
| `hidden_sheets.xlsx` | Hidden and very-hidden sheets are linted, counted against the cap of 10, and their state reported |
| `waived.xlsx` + `xllib.toml` | A waiver with a named approver suppresses a finding and appears in the report; a waiver with an empty approver fails CI |

---

## Test shape

```
tests/test_rules/test_XL002.py
    test_fires_on_bare_literal          -> exactly one finding, correct locus
    test_ignores_allowlisted_literal    -> no finding
    test_ignores_positional_exemptions  -> no finding for ROUND/VLOOKUP args
    test_no_other_rule_fires            -> full finding set equals expected
```

The fourth test is the one that keeps fixtures honest over time, and it is the
test most likely to be dropped under pressure. It should be generated from a
shared helper so that omitting it is visible in review.
